_current_scope.try_flow: Create a run; checkpoint; inspect sources; answer the saved request; export History evidence. Guided intake offers editable success, refusal and correction examples.
_current_scope.real_vs_demo: Synthetic records and offline interpretation; real HTTP persistence and Strands tool/session replay. No footage/audio analysis, real email or payment.
_current_scope.evidence_limits: Historical entries below are preserved, not exact-current-release acceptance. Hashes identify bytes, not truth; model identity only comes from serialized finding records. Human benefit and active time are unmeasured.
_current_scope.disclosures: README.md Pre-existing components; media source remains NOT_CONFIGURED.

baseline.what: The scene package as the corpus ships it, read by the offline lexical interpreter, with no human decisions recorded.
baseline.why_this_one: It is the configuration the live URL runs, so every number here is about the thing a judge can open. A Bedrock baseline would measure a different deployment and is reported separately in the README.

corrections.why: Written from memory of the corpus rather than from the corpus. The ledger covers five people and two visible assets, so seven rights findings is correct and six never was. No product code was changed.

rewrites.which_changed: the product contract, on purpose, not the expectation

contract_change.before: A publish that raised released its idempotency claim and re-raised, so a later idempotent publish of the same event retried it.
contract_change.after: A publish that raises returns a receipt with status unknown and keeps its claims. A later idempotent publish of the same logical effect answers that an earlier attempt remains unresolved and does not call the bus. Only an accepted or rejected outcome releases the effect claim, so a definite rejection is the retry the contract allows.

rewrites.retired_scenario: The bus raises on the first attempt, then accepts. The retry must publish and a third call must not reach the bus.
rewrites.why_not_edited_to_match: Setting those four literals to the observed values would have recorded 'a raised publish is never retried' as a pass for a case named retry and recovery. A disagreement is a failure here, so the retired expectation and its failing run are kept and the scenario is replaced.
rewrites.new_scenario: The bus returns a definite rejection, then accepts. The retry must publish, and a third call must return the saved receipt without reaching the bus.
rewrites.new_expectations_written_from: the WrapRun.publish contract, before the rewritten case first ran. tests/test_rerun_and_events.py::test_a_publish_that_fails_can_be_retried pins the same sequence.
